segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
[and Constans,] the younger brother.
And he left two sons:
Gallus and Julian.
Then Constantius, their uncle,
that is to say, the middle brother of their father,
because they were small,
ordered that they be educated in learning in the village of Macellum near Caesarea of Cappadocia.
And both of them became readers,
and they were building a church to Saint Mamas.
And when they grew up,
Constantius made one of them who was the elder, that is Gallus, Caesar in place of his father.
And after a little while he rebelled against his uncle who had appointed him,
and the king his uncle sent and killed him.
And his brother who was younger than he, that Julian, he also put into prison.
And afterwards, Queen Eusebia, his mother {OCR?: her mother / his stepmother}, requested him from the king,
and sent him to Athens {OCR?} to go and learn wisdom.
And there, along with the great Basil and Gregory of Nyssa his brother, and Gregory the Theologian of Nazianzus, he was studying.
And when Basil saw his movements, he prophesied that he would apostatize.
And he said:
"Woe to Romania,
what it is nurturing!" And that King Constantius, the middle brother, enlarged Amid,
and named it Augusta.
And that Constans, however, the younger brother who was in Rome, when he had reigned six years,
died through the treachery of soldiers.
And Magnentius the tyrant seized all Italy and Africa,
and was proclaimed (and was named) king in Sirmium.
And when the king, the middle brother, heard,
he went in haste against the tyrant,
and killed him,
and entered Rome in triumph.
And when he returned to Constantinople, he ordained Julian, the son of his elder brother, as Caesar,
and gave him his sister Helen as a wife,
she who was called Constantina.
And he sent him against the Gauls,
and he conquered and prospered.
And he became great and exalted and haughty,
and was proclaimed king by the Romans.
Constantius, however, his uncle, when he heard, trembled.
And he hastened and was baptized by Euzoius of Antioch,
and went out against Julian.
And between Cilicia and Cappadocia, at Mopsucrene, he died.
